title: The Instruction Hierarchy
full_title: The Instruction Hierarchy: Training LLMs to Prioritize Privileged Instructions
note: Model-level training so the LLM ranks system prompts above untrusted text. Cited as a baseline across the corpus.

title: StruQ
full_title: StruQ: Defending Against Prompt Injection with Structured Queries
note: Secure front-end separating prompt and data channels plus a structured instruction-tuned LLM. Named by 7 uncovered mechanisms' papers as the defense they tested against.

title: BIPIA
full_title: Benchmarking and Defending against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks on Large Language Models
note: Two defenses: black-box (explicit reminder) and white-box (boundary awareness).

title: Spotlighting
full_title: Defending Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks With Spotlighting
note: The provenance-signalling family everyone benchmarks against; named by 9 uncovered mechanisms' papers.

title: SecAlign
full_title: SecAlign: Defending Against Prompt Injection with Preference Optimization
note: The ORIGINAL SecAlign. The corpus already has 'Meta SecAlign', its successor; these are distinct entries. Named by 7 uncovered mechanisms' papers.

title: Attention Tracker
full_title: Attention Tracker: Detecting Prompt Injection Attacks in LLMs
note: Training-free detection from attention patterns on the instruction. Named by uncovered mechanisms' papers as a baseline.

title: From Prompt Injections to SQL Injection
full_title: From Prompt Injections to SQL Injection Attacks: How Protected is Your LLM-Integrated Web Application?
defense_name: UNNAMED: P2SQL mitigations (DB permission hardening + query rewriting)

title: System-Level Defense: Information Flow Control
full_title: System-Level Defense against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks: An Information Flow Control Perspective
note: Already cited BY defenses in the corpus (PACT and NeuroTaint both baseline against 'f-secure'/FIDES). Its own paper was outside the corpus until now.

title: Signed-Prompt
full_title: Signed-Prompt: A New Approach to Prevent Prompt Injection Attacks Against LLM-Integrated Applications
note: Authorised users sign sensitive instructions so the LLM can tell trusted instruction sources apart.

title: Can Indirect PI Attacks Be Detected and Removed?
full_title: Can Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks Be Detected and Removed?
defense_name: UNNAMED: IPI detection + post-detection removal pipeline
note: Also contributes a detection/removal benchmark. Directly relevant to the sanitizer family.

title: PromptShield
full_title: PromptShield: Deployable Detection for Prompt Injection Attacks
note: Detector plus a curation benchmark; targets the low-false-positive regime.

title: PIGuard
full_title: PIGuard: Prompt Injection Guardrail via Mitigating Overdefense for Free
note: NOTE: distinct from IPIGuard, which is already in the registry - an earlier probe of mine conflated them. Contributes the NotInject over-defense dataset.

title: InjecGuard
full_title: InjecGuard: Benchmarking and Mitigating Over-defense in Prompt Injection Guardrail Models
note: FLAG: near-identical abstract to PIGuard above, same NotInject dataset and same MOF training strategy, differing only in the reported margin (30.8% vs 30.4%). Almost certainly the same work under two titles - a rename across versions. Treat as ONE defense and retract the duplicate; do not count both.

title: DefensiveTokens
full_title: Defending Against Prompt Injection With a Few DefensiveTokens
note: Test-time defense with training-time-comparable robustness; already cited as a baseline inside the corpus.

title: COIECD
full_title: Discerning and Resolving Knowledge Conflicts through Adaptive Decoding with Contextual Information-Entropy Constraint

title: PI Against LLM-Integrated Mobile Robotic Systems
full_title: A Study on Prompt Injection Attack Against LLM-Integrated Mobile Robotic Systems
defense_name: UNNAMED: secure prompt strategies for robotic navigation

title: PromptLocate
note: Already cited as a baseline inside the corpus (the Relinking paper's source-sanitizer group). Its own paper was outside the corpus until now.
